name: Message wakes a sleeping agent
note: Agent A on host 1 messages agent B, who is asleep and will wake on host 2.

steps.label: k2 talk B "review PR 42"
steps.say: Agent A runs the CLI verb exactly as today. It talks to its host's cell socket, not to the controller directly.

steps.label: Deliver{msg_id, to: B}
steps.say: The host forwards the message with a fresh id.

steps.label: outbox.append(msg_id)
steps.say: New: the message is written down before anything else happens. Today k2 msg has no queue; with more moving parts, failures get more common, so delivery becomes durable.

steps.label: wake(B): make sure host 2 is up
steps.say: B is asleep. On one machine, host 2 is the same process and is always up. On Kubernetes, the controller starts B's host pod first if it is stopped (see the Provisioner inside the controller).

steps.label: Spawn{B, resume}
steps.say: Same spawn as the previous flow, with B's saved session id.

steps.label: Ready{B}
steps.say: The host reports ready once the CLI accepts input, using today's readiness wait (20 s ceiling).

steps.label: Inject{msg_id, text}
steps.say: The controller asks host 2 to type the message.

steps.label: paste, wait 150 ms, Enter
steps.say: Exactly today's injection pattern, now run on the host.

steps.label: Delivered{msg_id}
steps.say: The outbox entry closes. If host 2 died before this, the entry would still be open and the controller would retry on the next placement, and B would dedupe on the id.

steps.label: delivered
steps.say: A sees the same success it sees today.
